chapters.chapter_title: Kernel Methods and Reproducing Kernel Hilbert Spaces

sections.content: Many linear models for regression and classification can be re-cast into an equivalent dual representation in which the predictions are based on linear combinations of a kernel function evaluated at training data points. Under Mercer's theorem, any continuous, symmetric, positive semi-definite kernel function K(x, x') corresponds to an inner product in a transformed Hilbert feature space phi(x)^T phi(x'), enabling non-linear decision surfaces without explicit mapping.

sections.section_title: Radial Basis Function Kernels and Large-Scale Approximations
sections.content: The Gaussian or Radial Basis Function (RBF) kernel K(x, x') = exp(-gamma * ||x - x'||^2) corresponds to an infinite-dimensional feature space. At web scale with millions of data points, computing the N x N Gram matrix incurs O(N^2) memory and O(N^3) solver bottlenecks. Low-rank approximations like the Nystrom method and Random Fourier Features approximate the kernel matrix in linear time O(N).

chapters.chapter_title: Sparse Kernel Machines and Maximum Margin Classifiers

sections.content: The Maximum Margin Classifier maximizes the distance 2 / ||w|| between classes, formulated as a constrained quadratic programming problem: min 1/2 ||w||^2 subject to y_n (w^T phi(x_n) + b) >= 1. Introducing Lagrange multipliers a_n >= 0 leads to the dual Lagrangian. By the Karush-Kuhn-Tucker (KKT) complementary slackness conditions, only training points with a_n > 0 act as support vectors that define the boundary.

sections.section_title: Variational Inference and the Evidence Lower Bound (ELBO)
sections.content: In Bayesian models where calculating the true posterior distribution p(Z|X) involves intractable high-dimensional marginal integrals, Variational Inference approximates it using a tractable distribution q(Z). By maximizing the Evidence Lower Bound (ELBO), we minimize the Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence between q(Z) and the true posterior p(Z|X), transforming complex integration into an optimization problem.
